prompt.user:
Chunks:

[eng-repo-access-howto::s00p0]
All company source code lives in the GitHub Enterprise organisation. You sign
in with single sign-on, so you do not need a separate GitHub password.

1. Sign in to GitHub Enterprise with your company account.
2. In the IT service portal, open **Engineering > Repository access** and
   choose the team whose repositories you need.
3. Your team lead approves the request. Access is granted to the whole team,
   not to single repositories.
4. Add an SSH key or set up the GitHub CLI on your laptop so you can clone.

Write access to production infrastructure repositories needs a second
approval from the Platform team. If a repository you expect is missing,
check that your request named the right team before raising a new ticket.

[eng-local-environment-setup::s00p0]
This guide takes you from a freshly issued company laptop to running a
service locally. Do the steps in order. You need repository access first; see
the guide on getting access to code repositories.

[eng-code-review-process::s02p0]
- The repository's `CODEOWNERS` file adds reviewers automatically. At least
  one code owner must approve.
- Changes to infrastructure, authentication or payment code need a second
  approval from the owning team.
- You cannot approve your own PR, and an approval from someone who pushed
  commits to the branch does not count.

[eng-code-review-process::s00p0]
Every change to a shared repository goes through a pull request (PR) and at
least one review before it is merged. This page covers what authors and
reviewers are expected to do.

[eng-local-environment-setup::s01p0]
Install these from the self-service software catalogue:

- Git
- Docker Desktop
- Visual Studio Code or IntelliJ IDEA
- The GitHub CLI

If a tool is not in the catalogue, raise a software request in the IT service
portal. The Software Installation Policy explains how requests are handled.
